newsitem.title: DENMARK: SOCCER-OLD AND YOUNG BLOOD IN DANISH WORLD CUP SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OLD AND YOUNG BLOOD IN DANISH WORLD CUP SQUAD.

text.p: Denmark's new coach Bo Johannsen opted for a mixture of experience and youth on Tuesday when he announced his 18-man squad for a World Cup qualifier against Greece on October 9.

The experience of players such as the Laudrup brothers and goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has been supplemented by up-and-coming talent, including little-known defender Thomas Rytter who is set to gain his second cap.
Midfielder Allan Nielsen and forward Soeren Andersen, scorers in the 2-0 victory over Slovenia in Denmark's opening European group one qualifier a month ago, are also in the squad.
Goalkeepers: Peter Schmeichel (Manchester United, England), Mogens Krogh (Brondby).

Defenders: Jes Hoegh (Fenerbahce, Turkey), Jacob Friis-Hansen (Hamburg, Germany), Thomas Helveg (Udinese, Italy), Jacob Laursen (Derby, England), Marc Rieper (West Ham, England), Thomas Rytter (Lyngby).
Midfielders: Ole Bjur (Brondby), Bjarne Goldbaek (FC Copenhagen), Allan Nielsen (Tottenham, England), Michael Schjoenberg (Kaiserslautern, Germany), Claus Thomsen (Ipswich, England).
Strikers: Soeren Andersen (Aalborg), Brian Laudrup (Glasgow Rangers, Scotland), Michael Laudrup (Vissel Kobe, Japan), Peter Moeller (Broendy), Peter Nielsen (Borussia Moenchengladbach, Germany).
